briefing.quote: When agents begin acting for us rather than thinking for us, the efficiency revolution truly lands.

articles.title: OpenClaw v3.4 Released: Native Support for Multi-Agent Orchestration Protocol MCP++
articles.summary: The new release introduces cross-instance task dispatch, allowing a single gateway to coordinate 200+ agents simultaneously and tripling orchestration efficiency.
articles.detail: The OpenClaw team pushed v3.4 late on November 25, with the biggest change being an upgrade of its multi-agent orchestration kernel to the MCP++ protocol. The new protocol supports task-level dependency declarations, failure retries, and idempotent rollbacks, letting developers describe complex multi-role workflows in a single YAML file. Official benchmarks show that in a 200-agent concurrency scenario, task completion latency dropped from 12.6 seconds to 4.1 seconds. A newly added sandbox snapshot feature also allows agents' state to be saved and restored at any execution step, a major boon for long-running tasks and human-in-the-loop scenarios.
articles.impact: Maturing orchestration capabilities signal OpenClaw's shift from a personal productivity tool to an enterprise-grade digital workforce platform. Small and mid-sized teams can now build automation pipelines at low cost, while RPA vendors face mounting pressure of being displaced.

articles.title: OpenClaw Plugin Marketplace Monthly Transactions Exceed $8 Million
articles.summary: The third-party skill plugin ecosystem is booming, with top developers earning over $300,000 per month in revenue share from a single skill.
articles.detail: Official data shows the OpenClaw plugin marketplace reached $8.12 million in GMV in November, up 67% month over month. More than 12,000 skills are currently listed, with office automation, code review, and cross-border e-commerce operations accounting for over half of them. The top skill, "ClawSheet" (a spreadsheet agent), surpassed $300,000 in cumulative revenue share within 45 days of launch. The platform also adjusted its revenue split, raising developers' share from 70% to 80%, and gave search ranking boosts to skills that pass security audits. It additionally announced a $5 million ecosystem fund focused on supporting vertical-industry skills.
articles.impact: The plugin economy is replicating the App Store playbook. "Skill engineers" who can write prompts and understand business workflows are emerging as a new high-paying profession, unlocking the long-tail value of AI applications.

articles.title: OpenClaw Partners with Three Cloud Providers on Compute, Slashing Inference Costs by 40%
articles.summary: The official agent runtime now integrates cloud inference acceleration stacks, with enterprise subscription prices cut accordingly.
articles.detail: OpenClaw announced compute partnerships with three major cloud providers, domestic and international. Its hosted runtime, ClawCloud, will directly tap cloud GPU inference clusters, using KV cache reuse and request batching to cut per-unit inference costs by roughly 40%. In turn, enterprise seat pricing dropped from $49 to $29 per month, and the team plan added a flexible pay-per-execution billing model. The company also released a private deployment toolkit that supports running the full agent stack within customers' own VPCs, meeting compliance requirements in regulated sectors such as finance and healthcare.
articles.impact: Lower costs directly reduce the barrier to enterprise-scale deployment, moving AI agents from pilot projects to company-wide standard tools and accelerating the displacement of traditional SaaS.

articles.title: Weekly Skills Chart: AgentOps (Agent Observability) Tops the List
articles.summary: As agents move into production environments, demand for debugging, auditing, and cost-tracking skills surged 210% in a single week.
articles.detail: This week's skills market rankings show AgentOps skill packs claiming the top spot for the first time, with downloads up 210% week over week. These skills capture every tool call, token consumption, and decision path of an agent, generating replayable execution logs that help teams pinpoint failure causes and compliance risks. Second and third place went to "ClawReview (Code Review)" and "DocFlow (Contract Review)" respectively. Notably, 60% of this month's newly charted skills relate to "making agents controllable" rather than "making agents smarter," reflecting a market focus shift from capability to governance.
articles.impact: Observability and governance have become must-have requirements for scaling agent deployments. This skill category could produce the next generation of DevOps giants, making it a space worth watching for founders.

articles.title: "Multimodal Meeting Minutes" Skill Update: Supports 20-Person Concurrent Voice Separation
articles.summary: The new release adds speaker identification and real-time decision extraction, delivering structured action items within 30 seconds of a meeting ending.
articles.detail: Popular skill ClawMinutes has released version 2.2, adding voiceprint-based speaker separation for 20 concurrent participants, with accuracy for dialects and mixed Chinese-English speech rising to 94%. The headline feature is "decision extraction": it automatically identifies conclusions, points of disagreement, and owners from discussions, and generates to-do lists that sync to Feishu, Notion, and Jira. Official tests show a two-hour meeting is processed in about 30 seconds. The skill currently boasts a 78% repurchase rate among enterprise teams, the highest among productivity skills.
articles.impact: Meetings are moving from "recording" to "execution," directly connecting to collaboration toolchains and promising to significantly cut the lag from internal discussion to implementation.

articles.title: Security Skill ClawGuard Named Best of the Year, 99.2% Accuracy in Detecting Prompt Injection
articles.summary: The skill blocks malicious inputs, sensitive data leaks, and unauthorized tool calls, becoming a standard item in enterprise procurement.
articles.detail: ClawGuard was named "Best Security Skill" at the 2026 Annual Skills Awards. Its core capability is bidirectional inspection of agent inputs and outputs, covering three major risk areas: prompt injection, unauthorized tool calls, and sensitive data leakage. In third-party red team tests, it blocked 99.2% of 37 known attack techniques with a false positive rate below 1.5%. It has now been deployed in production environments by over 400 companies, with financial services accounting for the largest share. Officials announced that its detection rule library will be open-sourced next month for community co-maintenance.
articles.impact: Security is the passport for agents to enter core business systems. Open-sourcing the rule library will help drive industry standards and lower compliance costs across the sector.

articles.title: Apple Opens Deep App Intents Permissions, Enabling System-Level Agents to Call Third-Party Apps
articles.summary: iOS 27.2 beta lets apps expose structured capabilities that Siri and third-party agents can orchestrate.
articles.detail: Apple has pushed iOS 27.2 beta 2 to developers, bringing a major update to the App Intents framework: developers can declare "atomic capabilities" with parameters and return structures that can be called not only by Siri but also, with user consent, directly orchestrated by third-party AI agents. Apple also emphasized a "capability as permission" design, requiring an explicit user authorization record for every invocation, while sensitive capabilities (payments, deletion, contacts) are blocked from batch execution by default. The first wave of adopters includes productivity tools such as Notion, Things, and Drafts.
articles.impact: iOS is shifting from an "app collection" to a "capability collection"; an app's moat is moving from interface to capability quality, opening a new wave of distribution upside for independent productivity developers.

articles.title: China App Store Weekly Chart: AI Bookkeeping App Tops Chart for First Time, Paid Conversion Exceeds 12%
articles.summary: The photo-recognition, auto-categorizing bookkeeping app "XiaoZhangBen AI" logged over 2.1 million downloads in a single week, with strong subscription conversion.
articles.detail: According to Qimai data, the AI bookkeeping app "XiaoZhangBen AI" topped the China iOS free overall chart this week, with approximately 2.1 million downloads in a single week. The app captures expense entries via photo and voice, automatically handles merchant recognition, categorization, and recurring subscription detection, and proactively flags duplicate charges and abnormal spending. Its paid conversion rate reached 12.3%, far above the 3% average for utility apps, with an annual subscription priced at 68 yuan. The chart also showed that among AI apps newly entering the rankings this week, those "solving a single high-frequency micro-problem" accounted for 70%.
articles.impact: A narrow vertical wedge plus deep AI capabilities remains the best strategy for independent developers; the subscription model is once again validated in the utilities category and is worth replicating across other lifestyle scenarios.

articles.title: Apple Health Opens New API, Letting Third-Party Health Agents Read Trend Data
articles.summary: Developers can apply for access to de-identified long-term trend metrics to generate personalized health advice.
articles.detail: Apple has added a Health Trends API to HealthKit, allowing approved developers to read user-authorized, de-identified long-term trend data — such as changes in sleep quality, resting heart rate ranges, and exercise recovery indices — without access to raw granular records. All data processing must occur on-device; only aggregated conclusions may be sent to the cloud. First partners include the meditation app Calm and the fitness app Strong. Apple also updated its review guidelines, explicitly prohibiting differential pricing for insurance, credit, and similar services based on health data.
articles.impact: The "usable but invisible" model for health data opens a compliant channel for healthcare AI, with personalized health management poised to become the next high-value app category.

articles.title: Chinese-founded ContextOS raises $800M Series B for agent memory layer
articles.summary: The company provides unified memory infrastructure that keeps enterprise agents consistent across sessions and applications.
articles.detail: Singapore-headquartered startup ContextOS announced an $800 million Series B round at a $6.5 billion valuation, led by a global fund. Its core product is a "memory layer" for AI agents, offering hybrid vector and structured storage, conflict resolution, temporal decay and permission isolation to address the long-standing "amnesia" and "memory crossover" problems in enterprise agents. The company says it serves 120 enterprise clients with annual recurring revenue up fourfold year on year. The founding team hails largely from major Chinese tech firms and overseas universities, and the company is only 22 months old.
articles.impact: The memory layer is emerging as a standalone critical component of the agent technology stack, much as databases are to applications. This infrastructure track could produce a unicorn.

articles.title: Robotics startup Lingxi Hand unveils ¥50,000-class dexterous hand, orders booked into next Q3
articles.summary: Entering the humanoid robot supply chain with a low-cost tactile sensor approach, priced at just one-fifth of overseas rivals.
articles.detail: Shenzhen startup Lingxi Hand launched its second-generation dexterous hand, the LX-Hand 2, featuring 22 degrees of freedom and full-palm tactile sensing, priced at ¥49,800 — roughly one-fifth of comparable overseas products. The company's in-house flexible tactile sensors cut unit cost from thousands of yuan to the hundreds. Within a week of launch it received over ¥200 million in orders of intent, with delivery slots booked through Q3 2027. It also announced a Series A+ round, with funds earmarked for production line expansion and sensor yield improvement.
articles.impact: Dexterous hands are a critical bottleneck for humanoid robots; rapidly falling costs will accelerate robots from labs into factories and homes, triggering a re-rating of the supply chain.

articles.title: 「写代码不如审代码」：AI 代码审查公司 CodeSentinel 年收入破 1 亿美元
articles.summary: 专注 AI 生成代码的安全与质量审查，客户留存率高达 138%，成开发者工具黑马。
articles.detail: 美国初创公司 CodeSentinel 宣布年度经常性收入突破 1 亿美元，同比增长 230%。其产品专注于对 AI 生成代码进行安全漏洞、许可合规与架构一致性审查，直接对接 GitHub、GitLab 的 PR 流程。公司披露净收入留存率为 138%，企业客户超过 900 家。创始人指出，当 70% 以上代码由 AI 生成时，「审查能力」比「生成能力」更具稀缺性。公司计划明年进入亚太市场并推出本地化合规规则包。
articles.impact: AI 大幅提升代码产量后，质量与安全成为新瓶颈，「AI 输出的守门人」类公司正享受结构性红利，值得创业者关注。

hotProjects.quote: The opportunity belongs to those who act before the infrastructure takes shape, not to those who chase rallies in the news.
hotProjects.summary: Today's biggest trend: agents are moving from "usable" to "controllable, manageable, and scalable" — memory layers, observability, and security governance have become tracks attracting dual bets from capital and developers.

projects.name: AgentOps — Agent Observability Platform
projects.oneLiner: A new DevOps infrastructure delivering full-chain tracing, cost analytics, and compliance auditing for agents.
projects.whyHot: Once agents reach production, debugging and audit demand grows exponentially. Related skill downloads surged 210% this week, and investors have backed multiple companies in this track in succession. What enterprise CIOs care about most is no longer model capability, but "can we trace it and can we control it when something goes wrong" — exactly the value AgentOps delivers.
highlights: Token cost attribution with budget alerts
Supports private deployment and compliance audit reports
projects.riskTip: Big tech may build basic observability directly into model platforms; startups must build moats in industry depth and compliance scenarios.

projects.name: ContextOS — Agent Memory Layer
projects.oneLiner: Unified memory and knowledge-consistency infrastructure for agents across sessions and applications.
projects.whyHot: Just closed an $80M Series B at a $650M valuation. Memory is widely seen as the decisive capability for agents to become long-term assistants, yet model-native memory today is generally unreliable. As an independent middleware layer, its business model resembles a database — high customer stickiness and switching costs — a classic "picks and shovels" opportunity.
highlights: Memory conflict resolution with time-based decay
Multi-tenant permission isolation and data erasure
projects.riskTip: Memory-layer standards are not yet established; if major model vendors ship native memory protocols, middleware vendors may be forced to rearchitect.

projects.name: Low-Cost Dexterous Hands & Tactile Sensors
projects.oneLiner: Breaking the price bottleneck of humanoid robot core components with RMB-level flexible tactile solutions.
projects.whyHot: The second-generation "Lingxi Hand" is priced at just one-fifth of overseas rivals, with orders booked through Q3 next year. The biggest barrier to humanoid robot mass production is the cost of key components, and dexterous hands and tactile sensors are the hardest part. Once the domestic supply chain scales, it will drive a steep decline in the entire robotics industry's cost curve — vast upside potential.
highlights: 22 degrees of freedom + full-palm tactile sensing
Flexible tactile sensor cost cut to RMB-level
Intent orders exceed RMB 200M; capacity sold out
Expected entry into top robot makers' supply chains
projects.riskTip: The industry is still early-stage; end demand for humanoid robots remains unproven, and component makers are vulnerable to downstream production ramps.

projects.name: Security Review of AI-Generated Code
projects.oneLiner: A "gatekeeper" business auditing vulnerabilities, licenses, and architectural consistency in AI-generated code.
projects.whyHot: CodeSentinel's annual revenue topped $100M with 138% NDR, validating the thesis that "reviewing is scarcer than generating." As AI-written code keeps rising in enterprises, compliance and security liability have become top concerns for legal teams and CTOs — strong willingness to pay, high renewal rates, one of the few high-certainty tracks today.
highlights: Automated review integrated into PR workflows
Open-source license compliance and supply chain risk scanning
Localized compliance packages for the Asia-Pacific market
projects.riskTip: Entry barriers are not high, and platform-native capabilities at GitHub, GitLab, and others keep improving — watch for absorption by platform features.
